text: jia: FYI ArgoPay reported a spike in request timeouts from their Dedicated pool ~10m after the routing change. Seeing ~20% 504s. ops-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool-42 error-rate: 21% over 5m (route: north-america). automated trace: https://rwd/instr/abc123 sara: assigning owners and mitigations — who can take this? This looks like a P1 to our SLA. :warning: tom: I'll take ownership for the short-term mitigation. I pushed a quick routing patch to staging, PR: https://git.redwood/dev/repo/patch/987 — need a quick review + deploy. kevin: on it, will review in ~30m. If it's urgent I can prioritize. maria: can we fallback to the smaller model variant (quantized) for ArgoPay while the routing stabilizes? That buys latency headroom. tom: good idea — fallback is supported. I can flip a policy flag in ops to route ArgoPay -> model: rwd-q4 while we investigate. Minimal change: `opsctl routes update --customer argo --model rwd-q4 --force` (tested locally). tom: proposed timeline: 1) immediate fallback toggle — 15m 2) hotpatch routing rule rollback (if needed) — 30m 3) full root-cause fix (config + kernel selector tweak) — ~6h kevin: code review left one comment about a nil-check, should be quick. If you want me to merge before full review ping me, I can do it now. jia: SLA impact — CS told ArgoPay we're investigating and will provide ETA. If fallback reduces 504s we can avoid an escalation. lee-cs: I'm messaging the customer now with the 15m fallback ETA and will update with outcomes. sara: confirm owners: tom = short-term mitigation + rollback, kevin = PR review/merge, eng-platform (maria) = model-fallback gating, jia = overall incident lead. Please update thread when deployed. tom: deploying fallback now, will post status. :hammer_and_wrench: tom: deployed fallback at 2876501620, initial metrics show error-rate down to 3% for ArgoPay. Monitoring for 10m window. kevin: merged patch at 2876501880 after quick nil-check fix. maria: toggled model fallback gating to allow quantized variant for ArgoPay at 2876501905. maria: confirm telemetry looks stable, p95 down from 820ms -> 210ms for affected routes. jia: thanks team. Action items: - tom: follow up with full fix PR and rollout plan (due EOD) - kevin: add unit test for nil case (small PR) - maria: record the policy toggle in config audit - lee-cs: send customer update and invite to postmortem meeting tomorrow. sara: will schedule postmortem and assign follow-ups after triage. closing loop: if any regression revert immediately and @sara on-call. :thumbsup:
